chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who says to his wife, 'You are free from me, or released from me, or cut off from me, or forbidden to me,' and he said, 'It is not [effective].'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband saying 'You are free from me' to his wife?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that common declarative phrases such as 'you are free' or 'forbidden to me' do not constitute an effective divorce (*talaq*) unless accompanied by the husband's specific intent (*niyyah*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intentionality over mere verbal utterance, distinguishing between casual speech and binding legal acts. It underscores the principle that linguistic form alone is insufficient for marital dissolution without the requisite mental resolve.
